section: Solid waste, plastic waste, e-waste, biomedical and construction waste - rules and management
subsections: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s:
Consider the following rules in the field of solid waste management:
1. Municipal Solid Waste (Management and Handling) Rules
2. Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016
3. Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of their implementation or enforcement?
accepted.x: The MSW Rules were framed in 2000, the SWM Rules came into force on 8 April 2016, and the SWM Rules, 2026 come into force on 1 April 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the dates to establish the first and last items before fixing the sequence.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s:
The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 extended their applicability beyond municipal areas to which of the following?
1. Urban agglomerations and census towns
2. Railways and airports
3. Special Economic Zones
4. Religious and historical places
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The 2016 Rules cover all four categories, including urban agglomerations, census towns, industrial townships, transport facilities, SEZs and religious or historical places.
accepted.tq: Test the completeness of an extended coverage list rather than relying on municipal-area wording.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, waste was required to be segregated into which three streams?
o: Biodegradable, dry and domestic hazardous waste
accepted.x: The three streams under the 2016 Rules were biodegradable waste, dry waste and domestic hazardous waste.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the three-stream system of 2016 and the four-stream system of 2026.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents important provisions of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016?
o: User fees, spot fines, extended producer responsibility and prohibition of untreated waste in landfills
Only centralised collection and unrestricted disposal in landfills
Import for disposal, co-processing and absence of producer responsibility
Tourist fees, biomining of legacy dumps and four-stream segregation
accepted.x: The 2016 Rules provided for user fees, spot fines, extended producer responsibility for producers and brand owners, and prohibited the disposal of untreated waste in landfills.
accepted.tq: Identify the option containing the complete set of provisions belonging to the same rules.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s: The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 were notified under which legislation?
o: The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
accepted.x: The SWM Rules, 2026 were notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘which authority or statute’ method to distinguish the legal basis of environmental rules.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, every waste generator is required to segregate waste into which of the following four streams?
o: Wet, dry, sanitary and special care
accepted.x: The four streams are wet, dry, sanitary and special care waste, the last category covering domestic hazardous waste.
accepted.tq: Watch for the replacement of the earlier three-stream classification by the four-stream classification.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s: According to the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, landfills are intended only for which category of waste?
o: Untreated biodegradable waste and dry waste
Waste collected from bulk generators without processing
accepted.x: The 2026 Rules restrict landfilling to waste that is non-recyclable, non-energy-recoverable or inert.
accepted.tq: Find the precise restriction by rejecting the broad option that treats landfills as a destination for all waste.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding legacy dumpsites under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026:
1. Local bodies are required to map legacy dumpsites.
2. Biomining is to be undertaken within a time-bound framework.
3. Quarterly reports are required.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 2026 Rules require mapping of legacy dumpsites, time-bound biomining and submission of quarterly reports.
accepted.tq: Check whether all components of a compliance mechanism are included before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s: Which of the following thresholds is associated with a Bulk Waste Generator under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026?
o: 100 kg of waste per week, 5,000 litres of water per month or 20,000 square metres
100 kg of waste per day, 5,000 litres of water per day or 20,000 square metres
500 kg of waste per day, 10,000 litres of water per day or 50,000 square metres
50 kg of waste per day, 1,000 litres of water per day or 10,000 square metres
accepted.x: The specified thresholds are 100 kg of waste per day, 5,000 litres of water per day or 20,000 square metres.
accepted.tq: Match all three numerical thresholds; a change in unit or time period makes an option incorrect.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s: What is the duty of a Bulk Waste Generator under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026?
o: To process wet waste on site or obtain an EBWGR certificate
To mix sanitary waste with dry recyclable waste
To send all wet waste directly to a landfill
To transfer responsibility exclusively to railways
accepted.x: Bulk Waste Generators must process wet waste on site or obtain an EBWGR certificate as prescribed under the 2026 Rules.
accepted.tq: Apply the actor-duty relationship by asking what the specified stakeholder must do.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s: Which special financial and regulatory measures may be adopted by hill and island towns under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026?
o: Levying user fees on tourists and regulating tourist inflow
Exempting tourists from waste-related charges and banning biomining
Imposing only industrial cess on local manufacturers
Allowing untreated waste to be landfilled without fee
accepted.x: Hill and island local bodies may levy user fees on tourists and regulate tourist inflow as part of waste-management measures.
accepted.tq: Test a special-case provision that is easily confused with the general duties of local bodies.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s: The imposition of Environmental Compensation under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 is associated with which principle?
accepted.x: Environmental Compensation under the 2026 Rules follows the polluter-pays principle.
accepted.tq: Pair the named environmental instrument with its governing principle.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the earlier draft from the notified Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026?
o: The draft proposed 1 October 2025, whereas the notified Rules came into force on 1 April 2026.
The notified Rules were postponed indefinitely after the draft was issued.
The draft and notified Rules both came into force on 8 April 2016.
The notified Rules came into force on 1 October 2025, as proposed in the draft.
accepted.x: The earlier draft proposed 1 October 2025 as the starting date, but the notified SWM Rules, 2026 came into force on 1 April 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate the proposed date from the final notified date instead of treating them as identical.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s: The Supreme Court’s pan-India directions concerning implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 treated a clean environment as part of which constitutional guarantee?
accepted.x: The directions treated the right to a clean environment as part of the protection of life and personal liberty under Article 21.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among nearby constitutional Articles by linking the environmental right with life and personal liberty.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s: The Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016 treat construction and demolition waste primarily as which of the following?
o: Waste exempt from collection and processing
A resource requiring collection, storage and reprocessing
Radioactive waste requiring deep burial in every case
accepted.x: The C&D Waste Management Rules, 2016 require collection, storage and reprocessing and recognise C&D waste as a resource.
accepted.tq: Identify the positive management approach rather than the disposal-only interpretation.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s: The Environment (C&D) Waste Management Rules, 2025 are scheduled to take effect from:
accepted.x: The Environment (C&D) Waste Management Rules, 2025 take effect from 1 April 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year in the title from the date on which the rules become effective.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s:
Arrange the following stages in the hierarchy prescribed under the Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016:
A. Reuse
B. Prevention
C. Recovery
D. Safe disposal
accepted.x: The hierarchy begins with prevention, followed by minimisation, reuse, recycling, recovery, co-processing and finally safe disposal.
accepted.tq: Identify the strongest preferred option first and the final disposal option last.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s:
With reference to the Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016, consider the following statements:
1. Imports and exports of hazardous waste follow the Basel Convention.
2. Import of hazardous waste for disposal is prohibited.
3. Co-processing is placed above prevention in the waste-management hierarchy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because prevention is at the top of the hierarchy and co-processing occurs later, before safe disposal.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed hierarchy statement; the position of co-processing is the trap.
accepted.sec: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

accepted.s: The Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016 replaced which earlier rules?
o: Municipal Solid Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2000
accepted.x: The Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016 replaced the Biomedical Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 1998, which had ten categories.
accepted.tq: Use the predecessor-successor relationship to distinguish rules with similar environmental subject matter.
accepted.sec: Biomedical waste - colour coding, treatment

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the scope and compliance features of the Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016?
o: They cover all healthcare facilities, use four colour categories and require bar coding.
They cover only laboratories and require no tracking mechanism.
They cover municipal waste generators and require three waste streams.
They cover only government hospitals and require ten colour categories.
accepted.x: The 2016 Rules cover all healthcare facilities, prescribe four colour categories and require bar coding. GPS tracking was also introduced through subsequent compliance measures.
accepted.tq: Reject the options that import the ten-category system of the earlier rules or the municipal three-stream system.
accepted.sec: Biomedical waste - colour coding, treatment

accepted.s: The Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016 were amended in which of the following years?
accepted.x: The Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016 were amended in 2018 and 2019.
accepted.tq: Test the paired years directly; both years must match the amendment history.
accepted.sec: Biomedical waste - colour coding, treatment

accepted.s: In 2024, approximately how many healthcare facilities generated more than 800 tonnes of biomedical waste per day?
accepted.x: About 1.89 lakh healthcare facilities generated more than 800 tonnes of biomedical waste per day in 2024.
accepted.tq: Read the lakh-based figure carefully and distinguish it from figures differing by a factor of ten.
accepted.sec: Biomedical waste - colour coding, treatment

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct colour-treatment combination for anatomical waste, soiled waste, expired medicines and chemical waste under biomedical waste rules?
o: Yellow — incineration, plasma pyrolysis or deep burial
accepted.x: Yellow-category waste includes anatomical, soiled, expired medicine and chemical waste and is treated through incineration, plasma pyrolysis or deep burial.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive waste category and match it with its prescribed treatment.
accepted.sec: Biomedical waste - colour coding, treatment

accepted.s: Contaminated recyclable plastics such as tubes, bottles, IV sets and catheters are placed in which biomedical waste category?
accepted.x: Contaminated recyclable plastics are placed in the red category and are autoclaved or microwaved before shredding and recycling.
accepted.tq: Use the material-based distinction between recyclable plastics and sharps or glassware.
accepted.sec: Biomedical waste - colour coding, treatment

accepted.s: Sharps such as needles and blades are assigned to which colour category under the Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016?
accepted.x: Sharps, including needles and blades, are placed in the white, translucent category and may undergo autoclaving or dry heat treatment, shredding and encapsulation.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between red recyclable plastics and white translucent sharps containers.
accepted.sec: Biomedical waste - colour coding, treatment

accepted.s: Glassware and metallic implants generated as biomedical waste belong to which category and treatment combination?
accepted.x: Glassware and metallic implants are placed in the blue category and are disinfected before recycling.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive material pair with its colour and treatment rather than with the treatment of sharps.
accepted.sec: Biomedical waste - colour coding, treatment

accepted.s:
Biomedical waste may arise from the diagnosis, treatment or immunisation of humans or animals. Which of the following is included in this waste stream?
1. Blood
2. Sharps
3. Cultures
4. Discarded or expired medicines
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Blood, sharps, cultures and discarded or expired medicines are all examples of biomedical waste; anatomical and chemical waste are also included.
accepted.tq: Check each listed source against the broad definition of waste from healthcare activity.
accepted.sec: Biomedical waste - colour coding, treatment

accepted.s: According to the stated healthcare-waste composition, approximately what proportion of healthcare waste is general non-hazardous waste?
accepted.x: Approximately 85% of healthcare waste is general non-hazardous waste, while about 15% is hazardous, including infectious, chemical and radioactive waste.
accepted.tq: Use the complementary proportions to distinguish the large general fraction from the smaller hazardous fraction.
accepted.sec: Biomedical waste - colour coding, treatment
